description: The cross-user proposal workflow: a proposal, the reviews it attracts, and the boss's decision. Three ledger records, one lifecycle (draft → submitted → reviewed → decided), fail-closed on an out-of-order transition. Committed to the ledger exactly like an approval: dual-control signed, appended, hash-chained.
why: An agent that edits the vault can attribute its own work (a signed note), but there is no first-class object for 'here is a change I propose, here is what my peers think, and here is the owner's decision'. Without it a cross-user review is chat that leaves no auditable trace. This schema makes the proposal the unit of review: the originating agent's work, each reviewer's verdict attributed to a named agent and model, and the boss's approve/deny, each a signed ledger record whose order cannot be forged or rearranged.

scope.role: peer (a proposal is a peer's statement about its own vault)
scope.disjoint_from: the master vocabulary in contracts/tracking-schema.json. A peer proposes and reviews; a master does not. Adding these to the peer vocabulary and not the master's is what keeps the two disjoint.
scope.transport: see the `transport` section: the records ride the existing share ports 4201/4202 as a new message family, and a receiver verifies the bundle offline — no new port, and no new entry in capabilities.share_types.

transport.route: The proposal exchange rides the existing share ports 4201 (share-intake) and 4202 (session-transfer) as a new message family. It is deliberately *not* a share type: capabilities.share_types stays closed because a proposal conveys no knowledge read or copy, and adding one would give the narrowing relation a member it cannot order. No new port is opened (contracts/ports.json records the route on the share stanza).
transport.bundle: A wire message carries `records`: the ordered list of proposal/review/decision records exchanged so far. It is a bundle, not a ledger: the proposal stays on the proposer's ledger, each review on its reviewer's, the decision on the owner's, so no node ever records a foreign author's block (which would fail that node's own ledger verification, where each record's user signature is checked against *this* node's user key). `verify_proposal_chain` checks the union, so a receiver verifies a chain whose records live on other nodes.
transport.shared_ladder: Both ends verify with the shared ladder — shared/sparknet-proposal.py `verify_proposal_chain` — *before* signing anything. A refused bundle appends nothing.
transport.implementation: peer-node/services/sparknet-proposal-exchange.py delivers a signed proposal and returns a signed review/decision; peer-node/services/sparknet-share-regime.py recognises the message family (`accepts_message` / `proposal_route`) and refuses to run if this contract is missing.
transport.overlay_leg: The live cross-node exchange over the overlay is `DoD: confirm: user`: the development host has no wireguard interface, so the round trip is proven with two in-process nodes and only the in-process leg is claimed.

transitions.draft → submitted: `submit_proposal` signs the draft and appends the `proposal` block. A proposal that is not a `draft`, or that was already signed, is refused — the transition happens once.
transitions.submitted → reviewed: `review_proposal` appends a `review` block. Refused unless the proposal block is already on the chain and no `decision` block exists yet.
transitions.reviewed → decided: `decide_proposal` appends a `decision` block. Refused unless at least one `review` block precedes it and no `decision` block exists yet.

lifecycle.fail_closed: Every transition re-reads the ledger and refuses out of order: a review with no proposal, a decision with no review, a second decision, or a review after a decision is refused before anything is appended. verify_proposal_chain re-derives the same order from a bare list of records, so a received chain is checked the same way a local one is.
lifecycle.draft_is_local: `draft` is the un-appended record: `build_proposal` returns it, `submit_proposal` consumes it. Only `submitted`, `reviewed` and `decided` ever appear on the chain, because the chain records commitments, not intentions.

required_fields.stage: submitted (the draft stage never reaches the chain)
required_fields.title: what is being proposed, one line
required_fields.summary: the originating agent's work, in prose
required_fields.agent: the agent that produced the proposal
required_fields.model: the model that produced the proposal
required_fields.conversation: the conversation entries that produced it (the tracking.conversation shape: id, turn, agent, model, at)
required_fields.conversation_root: the RFC 6962 root of `conversation` (shared/sparknet-merkle.py), so the who/when/which-model trail is committed by the signature
required_fields.node_pubkey_b64: the appending node's identity public key, inline
required_fields.user_public_key_b64: the proposing user's public key, inline so an offline verifier needs no local key material
required_fields.user_key_fingerprint: sha256 of the raw 32-byte user public key, the label form `sha256:<64 hex>`; must equal the fingerprint of user_public_key_b64

signatures.user: base64, the user key over proposal_signable(record) — consent
signatures.node: base64, the node identity key over the same bytes — attestation

required_fields.conversation: the conversation entries that produced the review
required_fields.node_pubkey_b64: the appending node's identity public key, inline
required_fields.user_public_key_b64: the reviewing user's public key, inline

required_fields.agent: the agent that recorded the decision (attribution)
required_fields.conversation: the conversation entries that produced the decision (may be empty)
required_fields.node_pubkey_b64: the appending node's identity public key, inline
required_fields.user_public_key_b64: the deciding user's public key, inline

verdicts.approve: the reviewer accepts the proposal as it stands
verdicts.request_changes: the reviewer wants changes before a decision

signature.dual_control: Every record carries two signatures over the same bytes: the user key (consent / attribution) and the node identity key (attestation that this node recorded it). This is the same dual-control envelope an approval carries — shared/sparknet-provenance.py's `dual_sign`, not a new scheme. The `append_block` step then adds a *third*, independent node signature over the whole block header, and `hash` binds that signed block into the chain.
signature.message: proposal_signable(record) = canonical JSON (sort_keys, separators (",", ":"), UTF-8) of the record with the `signatures` key removed — identical to approval_signable.
signature.inline_keys: Both public keys travel inline (node_pubkey_b64, user_public_key_b64 + user_key_fingerprint) so a received record verifies with no local key material. Integrity is not identity: like a co-signature, a byte-intact record proves the bytes and the attestation, not yet who the signer is — the caller resolves identity against the registry or user.md. A record is therefore `verified` (internal consistency + order) and separately `trusted` (identity resolved), and this schema only owns the former.

verify_proposal_chain.input: an ordered list of proposal/review/decision records (the `data` of each ledger block, or a received bundle)
checks: each record is an object whose `event` is one of proposal|review|decision, with its required fields present
each record's `conversation` re-roots to its `conversation_root` (a tampered conversation is caught)
each record's `user_key_fingerprint` is the fingerprint of its `user_public_key_b64` (a swapped key is caught)
each record's `signatures.user` verifies under `user_public_key_b64` and `signatures.node` verifies under `node_pubkey_b64` over proposal_signable(record) (a forged record is caught)
exactly one `proposal`, and it is the first record; every other record references that `proposal_id`
at most one `decision`; every `review` follows the proposal; a `decision` follows at least one `review`; no `review` follows the `decision`
verify_proposal_chain.outcome: a list of problem strings; empty means a well-formed, in-order, signed chain. A forged signature, a swapped key, a tampered conversation, a missing proposal, a second decision, a decision before any review, or a review after the decision each yield a problem.
verify_proposal_chain.not_authority: A verified chain is not an executed change. A proposal records an intention, a review records an opinion and a decision records the owner's verdict; none of them edits a note or grants a capability. Acting on an approved proposal is a separate, grant-scoped write.

implementation.reuses: shared/sparknet-provenance.py loaded by path (which in turn loads shared/sparknet-authz.py and shared/sparknet-merkle.py by path) — this adds no Ed25519, no canonicalisation, no Merkle math and no key parsing. `dual_sign`, `append_block`, `canonical_json` and `build_conversation_root` come from there.
implementation.records_are_ledger_blocks: a proposal/review/decision is appended with shared/sparknet-provenance.py `append_block`, so it is a normal v2 block: header-signed by the node identity key, hash-chained, and checked by `verify_chain` like any other. The proposal events live in the peer vocabulary (contracts/tracking-schema.json).
implementation.transport: peer-node/services/sparknet-proposal-exchange.py carries the round trip as a bundle over the share ports 4201/4202 (see the `transport` section); live cross-node exchange over the overlay is `DoD: confirm: user`.
